capabilities: Seal notes automatically by hashing content locally and sending only hashes to a signed, hash-chained ledger anchored to Bitcoin
Show per-note proof status, sequence, and sealed version history with restore
Export portable .nanalproof files and issue paid PDF certificates and public verification links
Archive original files to a local git repository or optionally push them to your own GitHub repository
Verify proofs independently with a downloadable verifier, sha256sum and OpenTimestamps tools, or a public check page
disambiguation: Not a backup tool; the optional git and GitHub archives store originals, but the core job is tamper-evident timestamping and proof of existence.
extras: Desktop-only, with mobile support planned. Freemium: sealing works with a free API key, while PDF certificates, public verification links, and original-file storage are paid. The API host is fixed to api.nanalstamp.com and cannot be redirected. Sealing timing is fixed and not configurable.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to prove that a note existed in a specific form at a specific time with verification that does not depend on trusting a service.
